a new DDS design, DDS 3 and DDS 4, has been developed which has the following properties: (i) a Gaussian fall off in the initial wake function, (ii) an improved wakefield suppression at the synchronous frequency, (iii) a reduction in the peak wakefield at the synchronous frequency and (iv) an increased bandwidth.
The DDS1 model is a 9 parameterized structure which is a good approximation of the real structure.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of DDS 1, 2, 3 and 5 and the calculation of the wake functions for these structures.
the design of DDS structures and their use in NLC.
the design of damped detuned structures and with the development of a rapid method to calculate their wakefields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DDS design has been successful and that it is now possible to design a structure which has a dipole wake with a Gaussian fall off.
a DDS3 with an iris diameter of 1.8 cm and an equivalent shunt impedance of 5.2 MΩ/m would be a very good choice.
DDS 4, with a 1:2 ratio of iris diameter to cell length, provides the most effective reduction in the dipole wake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the DDS concept can be extended to higher frequencies and that the wakefields can be calculated in a rapid fashion.
the mapping function is a useful tool to design new structures and to rapidly calculate wake functions.
DDS3 and 4 can be designed and optimized in a fraction of the time taken by DDS1.

DDS1 is not a good model for DDS3 and DDS4.
a mapping function can be applied to a 9 parameterized structure to rapidly design a detuned structure.
a mapping function technique can be used to rapidly design DDS structures for different synchronous frequencies, thus avoiding the prohibitively large computational time of the MAFIA runs.
